case-sara.text: [Tearful] I got through work today, answered emails, smiled in a meeting, and then cried in the car because I missed him so much.
case-sara.suggestion: You kept functioning, and then the missing him hit you hard.

case-sara.text: [Hopeful] I want to believe I can feel better about myself, and for the first time it feels possible to work on that here.
case-sara.suggestion: You feel a little hope that this could be a place to work on how you feel about yourself.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I found an old photo while deleting things from my phone, and it made the breakup feel fresh again.
case-sara.suggestion: Finding that photo brought the breakup pain right back.

case-sara.text: [Angry] I hate that I still check my phone at night, like some part of me is waiting for his name to show up.
case-sara.suggestion: You hate that part of you is still waiting for him.

case-sara.text: [Sad] Mornings are the worst. I wake up for one second before remembering he is gone, and then everything feels heavy.
case-sara.suggestion: The morning starts with that heavy remembering that he is gone.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] My friends keep saying time helps, and I know they mean well, but I feel embarrassed that I am still crying this easily.
case-sara.suggestion: You feel embarrassed that the sadness is still so close to the surface.

case-sara.text: [Softly] I fill the day with errands and little tasks so I do not think, and then at night there is nothing left to distract me.
case-sara.suggestion: The busyness holds things off, and the loneliness catches up at night.

case-sara.text: [Embarrassed] When friends ask how I am, I make a joke or change the subject because I do not want to be the heavy one again.
case-sara.suggestion: You hide the heaviness so you do not become the heavy one again.

case-sara.text: [Tearful] I passed a couple holding hands outside the grocery store, and it felt like everyone else got picked for a life I lost.
case-sara.suggestion: Seeing them touched that feeling of being left out of the life you wanted.

case-sara.text: [Softly] Part of me keeps going over conversations, trying to find the moment he decided I was not worth staying with.
case-sara.suggestion: You keep searching for the moment he stopped wanting to stay.

case-sara.text: [Sad] I still set out two plates sometimes. Then I put one back before I sit down. Dinner is the loneliest part of the day.
case-sara.suggestion: Sitting down to dinner brings home how much you miss having him there.

case-sara.text: [Relieved] I spent an afternoon with my sister and actually enjoyed it. For a few hours I wasn't trying to work out what I did wrong.
case-sara.suggestion: It was a relief to enjoy being with her without blaming yourself for a while.

case-michael.text: [Firm] I spent the whole morning fixing other people's mistakes at work, and by lunch I was fed up with everyone needing me to clean things up.
case-michael.suggestion: You were tired and fed up with having to put everyone else's mistakes right.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] My wife said she is tired of walking on eggshells around me, and hearing that made me feel ashamed.
case-michael.suggestion: Hearing that she walks on eggshells left you ashamed.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] After I yelled last night, I saw her flinch, and then I felt sick with shame.
case-michael.suggestion: Seeing her flinch after you yelled left you sick with shame.

case-michael.text: [Tense and angry] When someone questions my decision in a meeting, I can feel my anger come up before I have even answered.
case-michael.suggestion: Being questioned in front of others brings anger up fast.

case-michael.text: [Embarrassed] Someone asked a simple question I could not answer today, and I felt exposed in front of the whole room.
case-michael.suggestion: Not having the answer left you feeling exposed in front of everyone.

case-michael.text: [Tense] I stayed up past midnight fixing slides because I could not stand the thought of someone catching me unsure in the morning.
case-michael.suggestion: You were afraid they would see you unsure, so it felt hard to stop preparing.

case-michael.text: [Firm] My wife's tone changes a little, and I am already bracing before I know what she is actually trying to say.
case-michael.suggestion: Her tone makes you brace before you even know what she means.

case-michael.text: [Tense and ashamed] I know I should apologize, but the second I do, it feels like I am handing her proof that I am weak.
[Tense] I tell myself I am only holding people to a standard, but underneath that I feel accused and cornered.
case-michael.suggestion: You call it holding standards, and underneath you feel accused.

case-michael.text: [Ashamed] At night I replay what I said to my wife, especially the look on her face, and I feel awful.
case-michael.suggestion: At night you replay her face and feel awful about what happened.

case-michael.text: [Frustrated] The deadline changed again. I spent the whole weekend finishing the report, and now it's as if that effort didn't count.
case-michael.suggestion: You're frustrated that you gave up your weekend and your effort seems to count for nothing.

case-michael.text: [Disappointed] My son asked his uncle to come to the school thing, not me. I know I've been busy. It still hurt being the one he didn't ask.
case-michael.suggestion: You understand that you've been busy, and it still hurts that he chose someone else.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] I am tired of sitting in meetings with my heart racing while everyone else seems normal.
case-jason.suggestion: You are tired of feeling so anxious while everyone else seems at ease.

case-jason.text: [Sad] I ate lunch alone again today and watched people at another table laughing like it was easy.
case-jason.suggestion: Eating alone while others connected left you sad.

case-jason.text: [Fearful] I wanted to say yes to game night, and then the fear kept building until I made an excuse and cancelled.
case-jason.suggestion: You wanted to go, and the fear grew until you backed out.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] When someone compliments my work, I smile, but inside I wait for them to realize they were wrong.
case-jason.suggestion: The compliment does not land, and you expect it to be taken back.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] I rewrote a simple text six times today because every version sounded weird once I looked at it.
case-jason.suggestion: Even a simple text turns into anxiety and second-guessing.

case-jason.text: [Anxious] I eat lunch at my desk because walking into the break room feels like stepping onto a stage.
case-jason.suggestion: Walking into the break room feels exposing, so you stay where you feel less on show.

case-jason.text: [Quietly] After I say something in a meeting, I spend the rest of the afternoon replaying it and cringing.
case-jason.suggestion: After speaking, you replay it and feel embarrassed.

case-jason.text: [Hesitant] In groups I go quiet so fast, and then I feel outside the circle even before anyone has left me out.
case-jason.suggestion: You go quiet and feel outside the group before anyone has said anything.

case-jason.text: [Trembling] When I had to introduce myself today, my hands shook, and I wanted the floor to open up.
case-jason.suggestion: Introducing yourself brought shaking and a wish to disappear.

case-jason.text: [Tearful] Sunday nights are hard because I realize no one is expecting to hear from me before the week starts again.
case-jason.suggestion: Sunday nights leave you painfully aware that no one is waiting to hear from you.

case-jason.text: [Worried] There's a team lunch tomorrow. I'm already thinking about where to sit and whether anyone will talk to me.
case-jason.suggestion: You're worried about finding a place at the lunch and being left on your own.

case-jason.text: [Pleased] Someone at work remembered something I'd told them last week. I felt glad they remembered me. It made the day easier.
case-jason.suggestion: Being remembered made you feel glad and helped you feel a little more at ease.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I can get through a whole shift at the hospital, talk to patients, answer my kids' messages, and still feel like I am watching it all from far away.
case-laura.suggestion: You manage work and family, but feel distant from what is happening, as though you are watching rather than taking part.

case-laura.text: [Worried] Since the divorce, I sit with the bills after work and keep adding the numbers again, wondering if I can keep the house or if I am pretending.
case-laura.suggestion: Sitting with the bills brings the worry that the house may be slipping out of reach.

case-laura.text: [Tense and guarded] When someone is kind to me, even in a small way, I notice myself stepping back before I know whether I actually want the kindness.
case-laura.suggestion: Small kindness reaches you, and you step back into guardedness before you know whether you want it.

case-laura.text: [Confused] I have been feeling depressed again, but nothing dramatic happened this week. Work was normal, the kids are fine, and I still feel like something dropped out from under me.
case-laura.suggestion: Everything looks normal on the outside, and inside you feel depressed, confused, and dropped down.

case-laura.text: [Slow and flat] I tell myself I want closeness, and then when someone actually asks me to come over or stay longer, I go blank and start planning how to leave.
case-laura.suggestion: You long for closeness, and when it gets close enough to touch, you go blank and look for distance.

case-laura.text: [Sad] A friend stopped inviting me over after I cancelled too many times. Part of me is relieved not to explain myself, but I also feel sad when I see her with other people.
case-laura.suggestion: You are relieved not to have to explain yourself, and sad that she no longer invites you.

case-laura.text: [Flat and guarded] I wake up tense before I even open my eyes, listening for whether something is wrong in the house, even though I live alone now.
case-laura.suggestion: You wake already braced, listening for trouble in an empty house.

case-laura.text: [Fearful] I avoid movies with fighting because one raised voice can make me feel scared before I can remind myself it is only a scene.
case-laura.suggestion: A raised voice on screen brings fear before you can remind yourself it is only a scene.

case-laura.text: [Tired] I keep trying to be normal at work, smiling and checking on everyone, but by the end of a shift I sit in the car because I am too worn out to drive home.
case-laura.suggestion: Holding the normal face and caring for everyone leaves you too worn out to go home.

case-laura.text: [Confused] I am not sure what I should talk about here. I could talk about sleep, the divorce, work, or my childhood, but mostly I just know I do not feel like myself.
case-laura.suggestion: There are several possible starting points, and underneath them is the sense that you are not yourself.

case-laura.text: [Flat, with a sigh] The bill came addressed to both of us again. I know it's a mistake. I'm still tired of being reminded, and then feeling nothing when I think I should be upset.
case-laura.suggestion: You're worn down by the reminder, and troubled that the sadness you expect isn't there.

case-laura.text: [Quiet] A friend offered to come over. I wanted company, then felt uneasy about having someone in my flat. I said no and regretted it all evening.
case-laura.suggestion: You wanted her company, but letting her into your space felt uneasy, and afterwards you regretted being alone.

case-carlos.text: [Hopeless] My wife and I keep having the same fight about my temper, and by the end we are both saying the same things as last time. Nothing changes no matter how hard I try.
case-carlos.suggestion: The same fight keeps repeating until you feel worn down and hopeless.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] I hate remembering the moment my son watched me slam that door. He went quiet so fast, and now I keep seeing his face when I try to sleep.
case-carlos.suggestion: Your son's quiet face after the door slammed stays with you as shame.

case-carlos.text: [Angry] My brother promised to help with the kids and then disappeared again. I had counted on him, and when he did not answer, I was furious.
case-carlos.suggestion: You counted on him, and his disappearing left you furious and let down.

case-carlos.text: [Worried] I am worried that if I lose one more job over my temper, my family will not recover. I keep doing the math in my head and seeing everything fall apart.
case-carlos.suggestion: One more blowup at work feels like it could make everything fall apart for your family.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] After I blow up, everyone gets quiet and careful around me. That silence makes me feel like I have become exactly the man I said I would never be.
case-carlos.suggestion: Their careful silence after you blow up leaves you ashamed of the man you seem to become.

case-carlos.text: [Tense] When things get calm after a fight, I feel nervous instead of relaxed. I start waiting for the next thing someone is going to say.
case-carlos.suggestion: Even when the fight is over, you feel tense, waiting for what someone will say next.

case-carlos.text: [Sad] My father is gone, and I still get angry that he never once said he was proud of me. It sounds stupid to want that now, but it still gets to me.
case-carlos.suggestion: Even after his death, the missing words still leave you hurt and angry.

case-carlos.text: [Confused] I know yelling scares my family, but in the moment it feels like the only way anyone hears me. Then afterward I hate that I used the one thing that makes them back away.
case-carlos.suggestion: In the moment yelling feels like being heard, and afterward it hurts that it pushes them away.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, clenching fists] I punch walls instead of people, and part of me thinks that should count for something. But I hate that it still scares them.
case-carlos.suggestion: The wall feels like holding back from worse, and it still hurts that it scares them.

case-carlos.text: [Ashamed] I want my family to feel safe with me. When they still flinch at my voice, it feels like proof that I have already damaged something.
case-carlos.suggestion: You want them to feel safe with you, and their flinching lands as proof that something is already damaged.

case-carlos.text: [Angry, then quieter] He changed my crew's plan without asking me. I got angry. Afterwards I was embarrassed that the lads saw how quickly he got to me.
case-carlos.suggestion: You're angry that he overruled you, and embarrassed that everyone saw how much it affected you.

case-carlos.text: [Low voice] My daughter went quiet when I came into the kitchen. I hadn't even said anything. That hurt more than another argument would have.
case-carlos.suggestion: It hurts that your presence alone made her go quiet.

case-nina.text: [Tired] Asking for help makes me feel guilty, even when I am exhausted. I start explaining why it is not really a big deal before anyone has even answered.
case-nina.suggestion: You feel guilty as soon as you ask for help, and start playing down how much you need it.

case-nina.text: [Worried] The car repair bill came, and I do not know how we are going to make it through the month. I keep moving money around in my head and feeling more overwhelmed.
case-nina.suggestion: The repair bill leaves you moving numbers around and feeling more overwhelmed about the month.

case-nina.text: [Torn] When I say no, my stomach knots while I picture everyone disappointed. Then I start explaining so much that the no almost disappears.
case-nina.suggestion: Saying no knots your stomach, and all the explaining nearly erases the no.

case-nina.text: [Sad] My sister forgot my birthday again, and I keep telling myself it should not matter because she is busy. But I was waiting for the message all day.
case-nina.suggestion: Her forgetting hurts, and you keep trying to talk yourself out of that hurt.

case-nina.text: [Apologetic] When I sit down to rest, I feel guilty within seconds. I start noticing dishes, laundry, messages, anything that proves I should get back up.
case-nina.suggestion: Rest lasts only seconds before guilt starts listing reasons to get up again.

case-nina.text: [Confused] I have been more depressed lately, but the boys are fine and work is fine, so I feel silly saying it. I keep thinking I should be grateful, not crying in the bathroom.
case-nina.suggestion: Things look fine from the outside, while you feel confused, depressed, and alone with the tears.

case-nina.text: [Ashamed] I explode sometimes, usually over something small, and then I feel awful for becoming the angry one after trying so hard to be patient.
case-nina.suggestion: After trying so hard to be patient, exploding leaves you ashamed of becoming the angry one.

case-nina.text: [Guilty] I dream about someone taking care of me for once, bringing me tea or telling me to lie down, and then I feel selfish for wanting it.
case-nina.suggestion: The wish to be cared for is there, and then the wanting itself starts to feel selfish.

case-nina.text: [Angry] A friend cancelled lunch at the last minute, and I texted that it was completely fine. Then I felt angry for the rest of the afternoon.
case-nina.suggestion: You sent the fine reply and then carried the anger and disappointment by yourself.

case-nina.text: [Tired] I do not know what to talk about today. There are too many small things, and I was hoping you could help me find where to start.
case-nina.suggestion: You feel tired and unsure where to begin with so many small things piled together.

case-nina.text: [Weary] I helped everyone else get ready for the holiday. By the time we left, I didn't care where we were going. I just wanted nobody to need me for a day.
case-nina.suggestion: You're so worn out from caring for everyone that what you long for is a day without demands.

case-nina.text: [Hurt, apologetic] They thanked the whole team at the school meeting, but left my name out. I know it wasn't deliberate. I still felt overlooked, and silly for caring.
case-nina.suggestion: You felt overlooked, even knowing it wasn't deliberate, and then judged yourself for being hurt.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] If you look away while I am talking, even to check a note, I panic that you are losing interest. Then I start talking faster, adding details, anything to keep you with me.
case-aisha.suggestion: When I look away, you panic that I am losing interest and try harder to keep my attention.

case-aisha.text: [Panicked] When a text does not come, my chest locks and I cannot breathe. I keep checking even though I know checking will not make it arrive, and each empty screen makes it worse.
case-aisha.suggestion: The unanswered text locks your chest, and every empty check makes the panic worse.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] I hear myself begging 'don't leave,' and then suddenly I am yelling like I hate them. Afterward I cannot explain how I went from needing them so badly to attacking them.
case-aisha.suggestion: You move from desperately needing them close to attacking them, and afterward the shift feels impossible to explain.

case-aisha.text: [Confused] I do not know what to talk about today; I woke up feeling wrong, checked my phone too many times, and cannot tell if I am sad or angry.
case-aisha.suggestion: You are unsure where to begin with a wrong feeling that will not sort into sad or angry.

case-aisha.text: [Worried] I am trying not to scratch, but when the panic gets that loud, my hands start moving before I have words for what is happening.
case-aisha.suggestion: The panic outruns words and moves into your hands while you are trying not to scratch.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] If someone cancels, I want to quit before they can leave again. Part of me knows they may have a real reason, but another part is already packing up and disappearing first.
case-aisha.suggestion: A cancellation feels like being left again, and part of you wants to disappear first.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] I hate myself after I blow up, even when I was terrified first; I keep replaying what I said and feeling disgusting.
case-aisha.suggestion: After you blow up, the replay turns into disgust with yourself, even though terror came first.

case-aisha.text: [Ashamed] I test people to see if they care, and then I hate myself for needing proof; reassurance does not last very long.
case-aisha.suggestion: You need proof that people care, and then shame comes when the reassurance fades so quickly.

case-aisha.text: [Desperate] When a session ends, the room tilts and I feel dizzy and left; I know the hour is over, but my body does not know that.
case-aisha.suggestion: The session ending feels like being left, even while one part knows the hour is over.

case-aisha.text: [Scared] I am scared that if I stop chasing people, there will be nothing left of me. Without the crisis, without trying to get someone back, I do not know who I am.
case-aisha.suggestion: Without the chase and the crisis, you fear there may be no clear sense of you left.

case-aisha.text: [Upset, speaking quickly] I wanted him to stay, but I told him to leave because I was ashamed of begging. Now I'm alone and angry that he listened.
case-aisha.suggestion: You wanted him close, pushed him away in shame, and now feel alone and angry that he went.

case-aisha.text: [Low voice] When things are calm, I don't know who I am. I'm relieved nobody is leaving, but I feel empty and almost miss having something to fight about.
case-aisha.suggestion: The calm brings relief, but also an emptiness that leaves you unsure of who you are.

case-david.text: [Controlled] When my wife calls me cold, I bristle because it sounds too close to true. Then I get angry at her for noticing the exact thing I am trying not to see.
case-david.suggestion: Being called cold feels painfully close to the truth, and you get angry that she has noticed what you try not to see.

case-david.text: [Frustrated] I know my father was impossible to please, but knowing that does not change how worthless I feel when I imagine his face.
case-david.suggestion: You know he was impossible to please, and still imagining his face brings up worthlessness.

case-david.text: [Defensive] When I feel criticized, I start listing everything I have achieved, because otherwise I feel exposed and ridiculous.
case-david.suggestion: Criticism leaves you feeling exposed, and achievements rush in to cover that feeling.

case-david.text: [Controlled] Praise feels good, then it leaks out; by the next day I need more proof that I still matter.
case-david.suggestion: Praise feels good for a moment, then drains away and leaves you needing proof again.

case-david.text: [Dismissive] When I admit I am wrong, I feel stripped down and small, so I argue even when part of me knows I caused damage.
case-david.suggestion: Admitting you are wrong leaves you stripped down and small, even when part of you knows there was damage.

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] When my kids cry, I get impatient, and then I hate how hard I sound when I see them pull away.
case-david.suggestion: You get impatient with their tears, then hate how harsh you sound when they pull away.

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] Since the affair came out, being at home makes me feel like a failure; even ordinary rooms feel like evidence against me.
case-david.suggestion: Since the affair came out, home itself feels like evidence that you have failed.

case-david.text: [Worried] I have been drinking more after work because it is the only time I stop feeling anxious and stop hearing my wife's disappointment in my head.
case-david.suggestion: Drinking quiets the anxiety and your wife's disappointment for a while.

case-david.text: [Confused] I do not know what we should talk about this week; if I choose, I will probably choose the thing that makes me look least exposed.
case-david.suggestion: Choosing what to talk about feels risky, with the pull to choose the least exposed version.

case-david.text: [Wounded but sharp] If I am just ordinary at something, I feel like I disappear; I would rather not try than be average in front of people.
case-david.suggestion: Being ordinary feels like disappearing, and being average in front of people feels unbearable.

case-david.text: [Controlled, bitter] They still ask my advice, but they gave the lead role to someone else. I can look gracious. Privately, I feel humiliated every time they praise him.
case-david.suggestion: You can appear gracious while feeling humiliated each time his success is acknowledged.

case-david.text: [Quietly] My wife says she'd like an evening where neither of us achieves anything. I want that too, but without something to offer I feel oddly worthless.
case-david.suggestion: You want an evening together, yet having nothing to achieve or offer leaves you feeling worthless.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] Most days I complete the routine and feel almost nothing behind my face. People speak to me, and I answer after a delay, like the words have to travel too far.
case-marcus.suggestion: You get through the day feeling numb, and even answering people feels slow and distant.

case-marcus.text: [Confused] I do not know what to talk about today; if I choose something, I am afraid we will open more than I can handle.
case-marcus.suggestion: Choosing where to start feels unsafe, like it might open more than you can handle.

case-marcus.text: [Hypervigilant] Nightmares leave me wired and empty, like the room is not safe; I sit up listening before I remember where I am.
case-marcus.suggestion: Nightmares leave you wired and empty, listening before you fully know where you are.

case-marcus.text: [Slow and flat] I avoid people because it feels safer than explaining why I disappear, and then I sit alone and feel worse.
case-marcus.suggestion: Avoiding people feels safer than explaining yourself, and then the aloneness gets worse.

case-marcus.text: [Worried] I have been drinking after work so I can sleep, and now I am worried I cannot sleep without it. I hate that something I do not trust has started to feel necessary.
case-marcus.suggestion: Alcohol has started to feel necessary for sleep, and you hate feeling dependent on it.

case-marcus.text: [Quiet and guarded] When something good happens, it feels far away, like it belongs to someone else; I know what expression I am supposed to have.
case-marcus.suggestion: Good things happen, but you feel little connection to them, even when you know how you are expected to react.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] A door slam can throw me back before I know where I am; afterward I feel embarrassed that a normal sound did that.
case-marcus.suggestion: A sudden door slam throws you back before you can place yourself, and afterward you feel embarrassed.

case-marcus.text: [Sad] A friend from the unit stopped calling, and I keep telling myself I did not want to talk anyway. But I still check the phone, and the silence bothers me.
case-marcus.suggestion: You tell yourself you did not want contact, and still the silence bothers you.

case-marcus.text: [Hopeless] Some nights I think nobody would notice if I did not wake up; I do not plan anything, I just feel that invisible.
case-marcus.suggestion: Those nights you feel so invisible that not waking up seems like it would pass unnoticed.

case-marcus.text: [Scared] I want to let people in, but every time someone gets close, I start looking for the exit. Then I end up alone again and hate that too.
case-marcus.suggestion: You want closeness, fear sends you toward the exit, and then the aloneness hurts too.

case-marcus.text: [Flat] I remember his birthday every year. Don't call anyone. I miss him, but speaking about him feels worse than keeping quiet.
case-marcus.suggestion: You miss him and carry the date alone because speaking about him feels even harder.

case-marcus.text: [Guarded] I want to sleep without checking the door. When I don't check, I feel careless. When I do, I feel trapped in the same routine.
case-marcus.suggestion: You want rest, but feel careless if you don't check and trapped in the routine if you do.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I still put two cups out. Seeing hers empty makes me sad.
case-arne.suggestion: That empty cup brings home how much you miss having Eva beside you.

case-arne.text: [Sighs] I fixed the gate yesterday. There was nobody to call outside and show it to.
case-arne.suggestion: Finishing it felt lonely without her there to share that little satisfaction.

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I miss her ordinary voice. Even asking where I left the scissors.
case-arne.suggestion: You miss the everyday sound of her, even those small questions.

case-arne.text: [Softly] Emma visits, but when her car leaves the house feels empty all over again.
case-arne.suggestion: Her visit brings company, and the quiet after she leaves hurts again.

case-arne.text: [Warmly] Tom made me laugh on our walk. For a while it was just good to be outside.
case-arne.suggestion: For that stretch, you could enjoy his company and being out there.

case-arne.text: [Frowning] I’m annoyed when people tell me to keep busy. I’m already doing that.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re working hard to get through the days, and that advice leaves you feeling unheard.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] I felt relieved not to listen for her at night anymore. Then I felt guilty.
case-arne.suggestion: The constant listening could stop, and guilt arrived alongside that relief.

case-arne.text: [Softly] I’m proud Emma asks me for help. It’s good to still be useful to her.
case-arne.suggestion: Helping Emma gives you a welcome sense of having something to offer.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Sunday dinner used to be our thing. Now I dread Sunday afternoons.
case-arne.suggestion: What used to be time together has become a lonely part of the week.

case-arne.text: [Frustrated] The paperwork makes me angry. Her name keeps turning into a reference number.
case-arne.suggestion: Those forms feel cold beside the person Eva was to you.

case-arne.text: [Tearful smile] Her old recipe has a grease mark where she always rested the spoon.
case-arne.suggestion: That little mark brings her way of being in the kitchen close again.

case-arne.text: [Tired] Some evenings I don’t need solutions. I just want someone sitting there.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re longing for company, without having to turn the evening into a problem to solve.

case-arne.text: [Half-smile] Breakfast is peaceful now. I hate that I can like the quiet.
case-arne.suggestion: The quiet gives you a little peace, and liking it brings guilt alongside that.

case-arne.text: [Briskly] I fixed the gate. Good job, really. Then I had nowhere to put the good feeling.
case-arne.suggestion: There was satisfaction in the work, and loneliness where sharing it with her used to be.

case-arne.text: [Looks down] I want Emma to visit, but I spend the visit telling her I’m managing.
case-arne.suggestion: You want her close, and showing you’re managing makes it hard to let her see that need.

case-arne.text: [Dry laugh] Forty-one years. Plenty of love, plenty of getting on each other’s nerves. I miss both.
case-arne.suggestion: You miss the whole familiar life together, including the things that used to irritate you.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Tom’s jokes helped. Then I felt I’d left Eva out of the afternoon.
case-arne.suggestion: Enjoying Tom’s company felt good, then seemed to put your connection with Eva at risk.

case-arne.text: [Careful] I don’t miss those hospital nights. I miss her. I need that understood.
case-arne.suggestion: You miss Eva, while you don’t want those exhausting nights back. You want room for that distinction.

case-arne.text: [Frowning] People admire how I cared for her. I’m glad, but that’s not all I was.
case-arne.suggestion: You value that care being seen, and want to be known as more than her caregiver.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] A day without thinking about her would frighten me. I also wish for one.
case-arne.suggestion: You want some ease, and worry that ease might mean losing something of her.

case-arne.text: [Softly] Her coat comforts me until someone asks why it’s still there.
case-arne.suggestion: It gives you closeness, and other people’s questions make that comfort feel judged.

case-arne.text: [Sighs] I don’t want another dinner invitation where I’m the empty chair everyone notices.
case-arne.suggestion: You want company without your loss becoming the center of everyone’s attention.

case-arne.text: [Warm, then hesitant] Helping Emma felt like myself again. Saying that sounds as if Eva stopped me being myself.
case-arne.suggestion: You felt something familiar in helping Emma, and worry that naming it could sound unfair to Eva.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Sometimes the sadness is easier than deciding what I want now.
case-arne.suggestion: Sadness is familiar; figuring out what you want in this changed life feels uncertain too.

case-arne.text: [Firmly] The quiet was good. Don’t turn that into wanting her gone.
case-arne.suggestion: The quiet gave you something you needed. That is different from wanting Eva gone, and you need the distinction heard.

case-arne.text: [Watchful] I moved the coat, then put it back. It felt wrong there. I can’t tell you why.
case-arne.suggestion: Something felt wrong about moving it, though the meaning isn’t clear yet. We can leave that open.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I miss her. I’m also angry about some things. Don’t tidy that up for me.
case-arne.suggestion: You need room for the love and the anger without my smoothing either away.

case-arne.text: [Dryly] I know I matter to Emma. That doesn’t stop an empty Sunday being empty.
case-arne.suggestion: Knowing you matter doesn’t supply the company you miss on Sunday.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] It’s not guilt exactly. More as though enjoying myself has nowhere to belong.
case-arne.suggestion: The enjoyment feels out of place in this changed life, rather than simply wrong. Is that closer?

case-arne.text: [Steady] I was tired of the care. I don’t need permission to say that, but I need you not to flinch.
case-arne.suggestion: You know the exhaustion was real. You need me to hear it plainly and stay with you.

case-arne.text: [Warm, then guarded] Tom and I laughed. It was ordinary. Please don’t make it a milestone.
case-arne.suggestion: An ordinary good moment with your friend, which you want left at its own size.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I don’t want her back as ill as she was. I want her, and there’s no way to have that.
case-arne.suggestion: You want Eva, without that suffering. Neither is available, and the longing has nowhere simple to land.

case-arne.text: [Careful] I’m not lonely every time I’m alone. Sometimes it’s the visitors who leave me lonely.
case-arne.suggestion: Being alone can feel right; feeling unseen in company can be the lonelier part.

case-arne.text: [Flatly] I’m not sure I feel anything about the photograph today. That doesn’t frighten me.
case-arne.suggestion: Today there may be no clear feeling there, and you don’t need me to turn that into a concern.

case-arne.text: [Firmly] I want practical help. Calling it avoidance makes me want to leave.
case-arne.suggestion: The practical need is real. Having it explained away leaves you feeling unheard here.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Yesterday I wanted company. Today Tom called and I let it ring. I don’t know what to make of myself.
case-arne.suggestion: What you want can feel different from one day to the next, and that leaves you unsure how to understand yourself.

case-mia.text: [Sad] I used to draw all evening. Now I put the pencil down before I’m ready.
case-mia.suggestion: You still want to draw, and it hurts to stop before you’ve had enough.

case-mia.text: [Frustrated] Alex opened the jar before I’d even asked. I wanted to try.
case-mia.suggestion: You wanted a chance to decide whether you needed help.

case-mia.text: [Angry] They saw me laughing at lunch and assumed I could work the whole afternoon.
case-mia.suggestion: Being cheerful got mistaken for having energy you didn’t have.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m frightened of making plans. I don’t know what tomorrow will be like.
case-mia.suggestion: You want something to look forward to, with no certainty that you can manage it.

case-mia.text: [Tearful] I miss being the person who offered to help.
case-mia.suggestion: You miss having that familiar way to contribute.

case-mia.text: [Relieved] Sam asked what would help instead of deciding for me.
case-mia.suggestion: It was a relief to have your own answer matter.

case-mia.text: [Sad] Ella meant well. But when she said I looked fine, I felt completely alone.
case-mia.suggestion: Her reassurance left the hard part of your day unseen.

case-mia.text: [Tired] Explaining why I need the stool takes almost as much energy as standing.
case-mia.suggestion: Even getting the adjustment costs energy you need to save.

case-mia.text: [Guilty] I snapped at Alex. I was hurting, but I still hate how I spoke.
case-mia.suggestion: You were in pain, and you’re upset about hurting him with your words.

case-mia.text: [Warmly] Today I explained a painting to a visitor. For a while, I felt like myself.
case-mia.suggestion: Sharing what you know gave you a familiar sense of being yourself.

case-mia.text: [Disappointed] I wanted to go, and I needed to stay home. Both were true.
case-mia.suggestion: Staying home was necessary, and it still meant missing something you wanted.

case-mia.text: [Steady] I want help carrying the bag. I don’t want someone choosing what goes in it.
case-mia.suggestion: You want help with the weight while keeping the decisions yours.

case-mia.text: [Half-smiles] Alex means well. I’m grateful right up until he starts answering for me.
case-mia.suggestion: You welcome his care, and lose something important when your own answer gets replaced.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I cancelled and felt relieved. Then I pictured them all laughing without me.
case-mia.suggestion: Staying home gave you needed relief, alongside the ache of being left out.

case-mia.text: [Brisk, voice catches] Three workdays is sensible. I know that. I hate needing it to be sensible.
case-mia.suggestion: You understand the adjustment, and still grieve having to make it.

case-mia.text: [Uneasy] When Sam notices I’m tired, I feel cared for and watched.
case-mia.suggestion: His attention can feel supportive and leave you exposed at the same time.

case-mia.text: [Dry laugh] I’m the reliable one. Except I can’t reliably say whether I’ll come.
case-mia.suggestion: Being dependable still matters to you, while your capacity won’t follow a promise.

case-mia.text: [Frustrated] Ella says I should ask. Then I feel like her whole visit becomes my needs.
case-mia.suggestion: You want to ask, without losing the give-and-take of being sisters.

case-mia.text: [Sad, then shrugs] I still draw. Just less. So I shouldn’t complain, should I?
case-mia.suggestion: Drawing is still there, and the amount you’ve lost still hurts.

case-mia.text: [Angry, then guilty] I wanted Alex to leave the plants alone. Now he won’t offer at all.
case-mia.suggestion: You wanted a choice about that help, and now miss having the offer.

case-mia.text: [Hesitates] I like a good day. I almost don’t trust it.
case-mia.suggestion: Enjoying the day is harder when you can’t count on the next one being like it.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] They praised me for getting through the tour. I wanted them to notice the painting.
case-mia.suggestion: You wanted your work to be seen, rather than just your effort to endure it.

case-mia.text: [Tense] I’m angry about the chair, but I don’t want to become the angry person at work.
case-mia.suggestion: You need that limit respected and worry that speaking up will become all they see.

case-mia.text: [Warm, then unsure] Alex waited for me to choose. I liked it, but it felt strangely slow.
case-mia.suggestion: Having room to decide felt good and unfamiliar enough to be a little awkward.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I wanted him there. I didn’t want him doing everything. I can’t make that come out kindly.
case-mia.suggestion: You want his company and room to choose, and struggle to say both without hurting him.

case-mia.text: [Corrects, then pauses] Not helpless. Tired of explaining. There’s a difference.
case-mia.suggestion: It’s the repeated explaining that wears you down, not a sense that you can’t do anything.

case-mia.text: [Dryly] I wanted the painting noticed. I also wanted someone to notice I’d managed to be there.
case-mia.suggestion: You wanted your work seen and the effort of being there understood, without one replacing the other.

case-mia.text: [Hesitates] Ella asked first. I still bristled. I don’t have a neat reason.
case-mia.suggestion: Even being asked didn’t make that moment easy, and you’re not yet sure what made it hard.

case-mia.text: [Flatly] Rest was right. It wasn’t good. Please don’t turn it into something good.
case-mia.suggestion: It was the needed choice, and you still lost an afternoon you wanted.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I left the drawing out. Didn’t work on it, didn’t put it away.
case-mia.suggestion: You haven’t wanted to keep drawing or to close it away just yet.

case-mia.text: [Uneasy] I want them to believe the bad days. I don’t want that to be my whole introduction.
case-mia.suggestion: You need the limits believed without becoming only the person with limits.

case-mia.text: [Softly] Alex stopped offering. I got what I asked for, apparently.
case-mia.suggestion: The stopping didn’t give you the kind of help or choice you were trying to ask for.

case-mia.text: [Warm, guarded] The museum felt like home today. Don’t make me explain why I can’t stay longer there.
case-mia.suggestion: Today there was belonging. You want that heard without having to defend the limit on your time.

case-mia.text: [Quietly] I’m angry with Ella, and it isn’t all because she got it wrong.
case-mia.suggestion: The anger is real, and doesn’t fit a simple story of Ella having done something wrong.

case-mia.text: [Tired] I don’t know if I’m protecting myself or shutting everyone out tonight.
case-mia.suggestion: You need something different tonight, but aren’t sure what kind of distance would help.

case-mia.text: [Almost whispers] I’m still me. Saying that feels true and not enough.
case-mia.suggestion: Being yourself still matters, and those words don’t cover everything you’ve lost.
